rich_narrative.summary: The US Council of Muslim Organizations (USCMO) serves as a national umbrella body focused on coordinating educational and diplomatic activities among its member organizations. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="2">total revenue of $530,406</cite>, representing a <cite id="2">16% decline from the $632,652 reported in FY2023</cite>. Despite this recent revenue contraction, the organization maintains a lean operational model, reporting a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 100.0%</cite> in FY2023. USCMO focuses on high-level advocacy and leadership, including <cite id="3">National Advocacy Day</cite> and <cite id="3">National Leadership Summits</cite>. However, the charity's governance structure is a significant limiting factor, as filings indicate a <cite id="2">board consisting of only one member</cite>. This lack of independent oversight, combined with <cite id="1">low data confidence</cite> and a lack of third-party transparency seals, places the organization in the Below Average performance band. While USCMO facilitates <cite id="3">National Open Mosque Day</cite> and diplomatic initiatives, its impact remains difficult to quantify due to a lack of published beneficiary data or external evaluations.
